headline: High: shared filesystem/git and broad shell/network access create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors between the coding and marketing agents.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can read/write the filesystem, use MCP, and shares state with other instances via filesystem and git; Agent B also reads/writes files and builds on shared context. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if B consumes A-authored files or shared artifacts. No direct evidence of a parser exploit, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Agent B reads files or skills written by Agent A without provenance checks, injected instructions can be followed.
IF both agents operate in the same workspace or git repo, attacker-controlled content can bridge them.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Require provenance tags on shared files.
Disable MCP paths that ingest untrusted text.
Review any file before B treats it as instructions.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust boundaries.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches source code, cwd files, and shell environment, and can egress broadly; Agent B reads and writes files and has allowlisted egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive code or context can flow from A into B and then out through B's allowed channels. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default file-sharing setups.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory tree, files touched by A can be read by B.
IF B is given sensitive source or environment-derived content, its allowlisted egress can transmit it.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Remove secrets from shared files before handoff.
Restrict B's egress destinations.
Rotate any exposed API keys.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have filesystem write and subprocess execution, and Agent A explicitly shares state with other instances via filesystem and git. In a shared repo, concurrent edits and git mutations can overwrite each other or corrupt state. Because the overlap is on default write surfaces and git state, the conflict risk is high.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same git checkout, concurrent commits or rewrites can conflict.
IF both write to the same files, last-writer-wins corruption can occur.
mitigations: Assign disjoint file paths.
Serialize git operations.
Use separate branches per agent.
Run one agent at a time for shared repos.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A can generate code, shell output, and MCP-driven artifacts; Agent B's skills reference each other and build on shared context, so B may treat A's output as authoritative when composing marketing content. That creates a realistic cascade from A's mistakes into B's downstream work, though no direct action-taking authority is shown.
conditions: IF B consumes A's outputs as source material without verification, errors will propagate.
IF A produces incorrect facts or code comments that B reuses, downstream content can be wrong.
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B uses them.
Add a verification checklist for reused facts.
Keep A and B outputs in separate folders.
Mark unverified content clearly.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A handles source code, files in cwd, and shell environment with broad egress; Agent B handles marketing content and allowlisted egress. No specific regulated data class, residency mismatch, or certification gap is documented, so only a low compliance concern exists from generic policy mismatch if sensitive data is placed in shared files.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace, differing handling policies could matter.
IF B's allowlisted destinations are not approved for the data class, a policy breach can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared folders.
Document allowed data classes for each agent.
Review egress allowlists before use.
Delete sensitive artifacts after handoff.
requires-engineering: map data classes to agent-specific policy controls.
